constraints.meaning: At least one number, at most 100.
constraints.impact: Adding every subarray from scratch (O(n²)) passes here. The prefix array answers each subarray sum with one subtraction: O(n), the idea for bigger inputs and for range-sum queries.
Each subarray sum is at most 100 · 1000 = 10⁵, and the answer at most 100 · 10⁵ = 10⁷: int is enough. Because nums[i] ≥ 1, start = max(0, i − nums[i]) is always ≤ i − 1 or 0.

constraints.meaning: The subarray for index i ends at i and goes nums[i] steps back, but never before index 0.
constraints.impact: With pre of length n + 1 (pre[0] = 0), the sum of nums[start..i] is pre[i + 1] − pre[start], also when start = 0. No special case.

bruteForce.summary: for every index i, add nums[start] + … + nums[i] from scratch and add that to the total. A subarray can have up to i + 1 numbers, so this is O(n²). It adds the same numbers again for many i.
